description: Issue #839 AC1, in the HERITAGE `to` spelling of the declaration slot. `spec/grammar.md` gives the grammar four declaration slots and `to` is one of them; `spec/conformance.md:150` makes Heritage "alternate spellings only. It does not add new semantics", so `to foo` twice must be exactly as illegal as `define foo` twice — same code, same params, same spans, differing only where the shorter keyword moves the column (the name starts at column 4 rather than 8). The corpus is the stack-neutral artifact another implementation must satisfy, so a `to`-slot rule pinned only in `packages/runtime` would not be portable. The two bodies print different values so the fixture discriminates between last-wins, first-wins and the ruling's rule. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's.
